context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Stop writing order PDFs, which contain Personal Data, into the publicly served 'ftp/' directory. Write them to a private storage path outside every static or directory-listing route (for example path.join(PRIVATE_ORDERS_DIR, pdfFile)), and give them random, unguessable names instead of names built from the order ID. Serve them only through an authenticated route such as GET /rest/orders/:id/confirmation. On every request and every HTTP method, that route should look up the order by its ID, compare the order's owner (its stored email or UserId) with the identity in the verified session or JWT, and return 403 when they don't match, unless the caller holds a role authorised for that record. Ownership must never be decided by the filename or by an ID taken from the path or body. Also remove or lock down the static and serveIndex middleware on /ftp so existing order_*.pdf files can't be listed or downloaded without authentication, and move or delete PDFs already stored there.
